hypotheses.justification: The statement stays true without `hv`. `individualize_cst_eq` (rfl) shows the new `cst` differs from `p.cst` only on `[c+1, ec)`, where `i = p.pos[v]!`, `c = p.cst[i]!` and `ec = p.cen[i]!`. If `v ≥ n`, then `hp.posSize` gives `p.pos.size = n`, so `p.pos[v]! = 0`. If `n = 0` the goal is vacuous (no `i < n`). If `n > 0`, then `i = 0 < n`. `cstLe` gives `c = 0`, and `ltCen`/`cenLe` give `0 < ec ≤ n`. For `1 ≤ k < ec`, `cellCst` at index 0 gives `p.cst[k]! = p.cst[0]! = 0 ≠ k`, so no start `k` with `p.cst[k]! = k` is overwritten. Hence `Refines` holds. The proof splits on `v < n`: the `v < n` case uses the existing proof. In the other case, rewrite `p.pos[v]! = 0` and use `individualize_cst_eq` with `setCstFrom_getElemD` (side condition `ec ≤ p.cst.size` from `hp.cenLe 0` and `hp.cstSize`), then the `cellCst` argument. `IndivData` itself needs `v < n`, so this case bypasses it. `hp` is still needed.
